source_evidence: You pay the taxes on contributions and earnings when the savings are withdrawn. In a Roth 401(k) account, employee contributions are not tax-deferred but are made with after-tax dollars.
question: How do traditional and Roth 401(k) accounts differ in when taxes apply?
answer: With a traditional 401(k), contributions and investment earnings are tax-deferred, and taxes are paid when the money is withdrawn. With a Roth 401(k), contributions are made with after-tax dollars; account earnings and withdrawals are generally tax-free.
